title: The one-page creative brief: eight lines
hook: If a brief needs a call to explain it, the revisions have already started.
caption:
If a brief needs a call to explain it, the revisions have already started.

A creator or editor needs eight things on one page: the buyer, the message, the proof, the first two seconds, the ask, what must be in, what is free to change, and what the ad is testing.

Everything beyond that is theirs to make good.

The full template is on the last slide. Screenshot it and use it for your next brief.

Want briefs built from what your own ads have already proved? Link in bio. Follow @galvor.ai.

Slide 6: line eight, what the ad is testing. Slide 7: all eight lines on one slide in two columns. Slide 8: follow @galvor.ai.

slides.headline: The *one-page creative brief*: eight lines, no call needed
slides.sub: Screenshot the template on the last slide.

slides.headline: Long briefs get *skimmed*. Thin briefs get guessed.
slides.body:
A creator or editor needs to know who the ad is for, what it must say and what is fixed.

Everything else is theirs to make good.

slides.headline: *Who*, what, and why believe it
items: Buyer: one person, described in a sentence
Message: the one thing they should remember
Proof: the fact, demo or review that backs it

slides.headline: The *opening* and the ask
items: First two seconds: what we see and hear
Ask: what the viewer should do next

slides.headline: What is *fixed*, what is free
items: Must have: claims, logo, price, legal lines
Free to change: everything not listed above

slides.headline: What this ad is *testing*
items: The one thing that is new here
What we will compare it with

slides.headline: Fill it in. *Send it without a call.*
